name: Baseline analyst
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: The largest lever overall, but academia training a general-purpose foundation model is locked out by capital and data scale; only a narrow-domain, conditional version still has room
D01.late_modes: Training a general-purpose foundation model from scratch is already too late; capital and data scale overwhelm academia

D02.one_line: The fact that RLVR does not produce new out-of-distribution capability was confirmed by convergence in three rounds of the X7 debate, but reliable execution is a real industrial lever independent of new capability, which R1 underestimated
D02.late_modes: Directly applying standard DPO/GRPO pipelines is already too late; diagnostic research is still open

D03.one_line: The DGM 'cheap and effective' cost evidence was overturned by the errata check; AlphaEvolve is narrow-domain compounding at Google scale; the current state is still mainly compute-driven trial and error
D03.late_modes: Putting a new prompt or framework layer on an existing agent is already too late; the self-improvement algorithm itself is not too late

D04.one_line: Evidence consistently points to scaffolding value being absorbed quickly by models and vendor CLIs, which almost closes this road to academia
D04.late_modes: Building a general agent framework or harness is already very late; vendor CLIs have absorbed it

D05.one_line: The independent arguments at three tables, X1/X2/X4, all point to credible measurement being scarcer than R1 estimated: certification is separate from production, building one's own evaluation counts as a contribution, and self-improvement needs a compute-normalized metric
D05.late_modes: Running yet another judge-consistency retest is already too late unless there is a new statistical method

D06.one_line: Data and generalization are still the real bottlenecks, and low-cost hardware has lowered the entry bar for some algorithmic problems to a level academia can reach
D06.late_modes: Pure teleoperation data collection plus behavior-cloning replication is already too late; without a new algorithm it is meaningless

D07.one_line: Action representation (diffusion/autoregressive/flow) is still unsettled, and is one of the few directions still open at the mechanism level
D07.late_modes: Simply swapping in another off-the-shelf action head without a new mechanism is already too late

D08.one_line: That a representation exists ≠ that the policy uses it is still unconfirmed, but X3/X5 separated the 'imagination layer vs decision layer' cleanly and gave an executable causal/ablation design, making the academic path clearer
D08.late_modes: Directly using an off-the-shelf video model as a world model without representation analysis is already too late

D09.one_line: Simulation is one of the few areas where academia can get high-quality results with low-cost hardware, and credible sim-real correlation evidence already exists
D09.late_modes: Merely using simulation to generate more demonstrations of the same kind is already too late; without a new evaluation angle it is not enough

D10.one_line: Industry impact is huge but the field is locked up by fleet data and top companies with years of accumulation, so new academic entrants get poor value
D10.late_modes: Module-level improvements to end-to-end perception and planning are already too late; fleet data scale overwhelms them

D11.one_line: Benchmark scores are rising fast, but the real gap in spatial and video understanding is still large, and diagnostic benchmark work is a strength of academia
D11.late_modes: Chasing scores on regular VQA or grounding is already too late unless a systematic failure mode is uncovered

D12.one_line: Efficiency and distillation methods are the narrow opening where academia can still contribute mechanism innovation, but the model-level arms race belongs to big companies
D12.late_modes: Training yet another general-purpose text-to-image or text-to-video model is already too late; a few big companies have locked it up

D13.one_line: Mechanism-level problems are still largely open and the compute bar is low
D13.late_modes: Superficial case studies of models doing bad things are already too late; mechanism-level work is not too late

D14.one_line: FlashAttention-style narrow-and-deep systems contributions can still be made by academia and adopted industry-wide; kept brief

D15.one_line: AlphaEvolve shows that narrow, automatically verifiable settings can yield results, but on most real tasks deep models still cannot beat simple baselines; kept brief

D16.one_line: Generative recommendation has industrial deployment but a markedly higher compute cost; kept brief

lever_reason: World models/WAM are still the core bottleneck of physical AI; X7 reconfirmed the reliable-execution lever of RLVR as real value independent of new capability, so L2 is raised

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, ground-truth evaluation (not pure judge), a complementary team of 2 or more, month-scale compute, open weights that can be adopted; for training a brand-new foundation model all five are indispensable

cruxes.question: Is the core lever of physical-AI progress world models/WAM, or evaluation and verification?
cruxes.my_position: Evaluation is a certification/error-correction mechanism and does not produce capability, but it is scarcer than I estimated in R1, and the score gap has narrowed
cruxes.would_change_if: In 2027-28 an independent team confirms on long-horizon real-robot tasks that the representation is really used by the policy

cruxes.question: Can academia still make original contributions on world models that industry adopts?
cruxes.my_position: Yes, but only narrow-and-deep representation or causal analysis; training a whole model needs cross-institution collaboration including industry resources
cruxes.would_change_if: If a compute-limited, purely academic team produces, within twelve months, a new training objective that industry adopts

cruxes.question: Diagnostic-evaluation research is easy to publish, but does it really have impact, or is it a comfort zone?
cruxes.my_position: The most critical factual anchor of the whole X7 table was an academic diagnostic paper; its impact is more real than I estimated in R1, not merely easy to publish
cruxes.would_change_if: If some judge-bias correction method is actually adopted by several independent evaluation platforms

taste_advice: Prefer problems that can be falsified and have a manageable compute bar; in this round's debate, the arguments that finally persuaded were of this kind, not narrative or seniority

changes.because: Mechanism conclusion converged on in the three-round X7 debate + overtime (Huang vs. Karpathy); errata_B table 1 items 1-3 confirm the three core facts about Yue et al./s1/DeepSeek-R1
changes.why: The diagnostic conclusion that RLVR does not produce new out-of-distribution capability was itself established by a top academic paper (Yue et al., NeurIPS 2025 oral), which shows that this kind of diagnostic research is doable by academia and carries weight; reliable execution is a real industrial lever independent of new capability, and R1 underestimated academic_edge/bottleneck

changes.because: errata_B table 1 item 8: the Darwin Gödel Machine cost figure of $22,000 over two weeks was not verified first-hand and comes from a secondhand blog with no cited source; the X4 table confirmed METR's 70-90% compute-spend data
changes.why: The strongest cheap-success-case evidence I used in R1 to support the 'vacuum opportunity' does not hold; the most solid evidence available shows the current state is still mainly compute-driven trial and error, not driven by methodological insight, so academic_edge and window are lowered

changes.because: X1 table consensus (evaluation certifies and does not produce; K3: certification ≠ production); X2 table consensus (when no ready-made evaluation exists, building one counts as a contribution); X4 table's new framing (self-improvement needs a compute-normalized metric, which is an evaluation-science question)
changes.why: The independent content of the three tables all points to credible measurement being scarcer and offering more room for academia than I estimated in R1, and the fact that open-world robots lack a self-generated right/wrong signal strengthens its bottleneck character

learned: I underestimated evaluation/measurement work in R1: X1 confirmed that evaluation is a mechanism of certification rather than of producing capability, but X2/X4 showed respectively that 'self-built evaluation' and 'compute-normalized self-improvement metrics' are themselves truly scarce academic contributions, which pushed D05 up. The three-round X7 debate plus overtime fully converged the factual dispute over RLVR (it produces no new out-of-distribution patterns); what remains is the value question of how high reliable execution should score, which I consider a real industrial lever underestimated in R1, so I raised D02. X4 showed that the hardest 'cheap and effective' evidence for self-improvement (the Darwin Gödel Machine cost) does not hold after the errata check, and the current state is still mainly compute-driven trial and error, so I lowered D03. This round's self-check found that OpenVLA was actually a collaboration of 18 people across 6 institutions (including three teams with industry backgrounds: Google DeepMind, Toyota Research Institute and Physical Intelligence), not the small purely academic team precedent that R1 implied; this weakened the argument for Q2, so I lowered the Q2 score and added C3 (team) as a necessary condition. The core uncertainty on D08 (a representation existing ≠ being used) was repeatedly and independently confirmed by X3/X5 as still open; it did not change the scores but strengthened my confidence in designing causal-intervention/ablation subproblems.
